text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday morning's German newspapers:

- Finance Minister Waigel says further 3 billion marks need to be cut from 1997 budget, adding one billion need be cut from Labour Ministry budget and another 2 billion marks from all other ministry budgets. New credit needs for 1997 will not exceed the already planned 56.5 billion marks.
- Cabinet approves designs for new health care insurance.
- Government's move to Berlin in 1999 may be delayed due to lack of office space for members of parliament and delays in building new housing for government workers.
- Cabinet approves import ban for certain risky French beef products that may contain BSE.
- NATO Secretary General Solana hopes for German participation in IFOR 2, praises German contribution in Bosnian peace efforts
- Siemens share price plunges after company announces record profits. Traders say company's expectations that there will be no further profit improvements in 1996/97 responsible.
- Airbus receives large order for 120 A-320 planes from US Air.
- German Defence Minister Ruehe says Bonn wants to send 3,000 soldiers to Bosnia.
- FDP parliamentary leader Hermann Otto Solms says the coalition government nearly collapsed on Tuesday in the dispute over the budget.
- Economists expect slight increase in unemployment in October. Federal Labour Office in Nuremberg to present data on Thursday.

- An asylum-seeker from India whose request was rejected was held by border authorities for eight months in small room at Frankfurt airport. Court rules that asylum-seekers can be held only a maximum of 19 days at airport.
- The coalition nearly fell apart in dispute over solidarity tax surcharge.
- Defence ministry expects 2 billion mark budget deficit for 1997.
